data.description:
Spike: prove (or refute) that the advance loop can hold WIP=2 — two tasks occupying active stages concurrently, two implementer sub-agents in two worktrees under ONE tick and ONE orchestrator — without corrupting board state. Filed per docs/strategy/11-second-developer-decision.md §4 and §9.7 (priority raised medium→high there: at ~88% line utilization with a 4-wide D1 ready queue, WIP is the only throughput term left in throughput ≈ WIP ÷ cycle-time; at ~30 remaining D1 stage-lifecycles, lanes break even inside their first day). §9.8 makes THIS TASK'S WRITTEN RESULT the next re-decision point — pair retention (developer-lena / qa-ruben, hired 2026-09-02) is re-taken against it if the spike fails — so the result must be decision-grade in either direction.

WHAT THE SPIKE MUST ANSWER
1. Can two tasks hold active stages concurrently with zero board-state corruption? (Corruption is defined checkably under SHIPS CLEAN below — not vibes.)
2. What exactly must change, delivered as concrete diffs/wording, in:
   (a) .claude/commands/advance.md — step 0's lock protocol and the Bounds section ("one tick advances one task by one lifecycle stage" is one of the two mechanisms pinning WIP=1; the single-flight lock is the other, and the lock STAYS);
   (b) CLAUDE.md Operating Modes + Git Methodology worktree/concurrency rules — metawork: the spike DELIVERS exact proposed wording, the metawork layer applies it, employees never edit those files;
   (c) the Employee Execution Model's board-write ownership. Under lanes, implementer sub-agents are forbidden to touch .lattice/ entirely; the orchestrator becomes the SOLE board writer, serializing every .lattice/ mutation and every master commit. Today employees post their own Lattice comments, so the spike must design the relay — likely: sub-agents hand back breadcrumb text, the orchestrator executes the write attributed to the authoring employee (consistent with CLAUDE.md: attribution follows authorship of the decision, not the keystroke). Validate it, do not assume it.
3. Tick-duration budget. Watcher-fired ticks are SIGTERMed at 30 min (tickTimeoutMin, apps/chat/watch/advance-watcher.mjs), the lock heartbeat obligation is a rewrite every 30 min, staleness is 45. D1-scale implementation stages have run 70–381 min. Does a fanned tick fit any watcher budget at all, or are lanes live-loop/manual-session-only at first? Answer explicitly; if timeout numbers change, that is watcher config + launchd plist — a board-visible ops change, not a silent constant edit.
4. Does the fan pay? Measure the fanned trial's wall clock against the same two stages run serially. The complexity is justified only if the number says so.

INVARIANTS THE SPIKE MUST NOT BREAK (design constraints, not suggestions)
- Task claims and status transitions happen in the MAIN checkout only; the main checkout never leaves master (two-plane rule).
- Task branches carry code only — zero .lattice/ writes on any task branch, ever.
- One worktree per in-flight task; one agent per task at a time. Lanes mean more tasks in flight, never more agents on one task.
- The single-flight lock stays. Lanes live UNDER one lock-holding tick. The watcher's lock/nonce contract (source+pid+nonce adoption in step 0, settle() release, nonce-blind staleness) is unchanged unless the spike names the change precisely and argues why it is safe.
- Per the watcher README: the lock is etiquette, not a correctness invariant. Correctness must live in Lattice claims plus main-checkout serialization, and the spike proves that it does.

FAILURE MODES ALREADY LIVED — the spike's job is to prove lanes cannot resurrect them
- AS-26 working-directory hazard (CLAUDE.md, Git Methodology): a cd into a worktree silently redirected lattice writes onto the task branch, and every read afterward looked correct. Two concurrent sub-agents double the exposure and the failure is silent — this is WHY the sole-board-writer design exists.
- 2026-08-31 duplicate CEO scoring pass (docs/strategy/04-scores-ceo.md, Drafting record): the single-flight lock was installed after concurrency cost us duplicated work once. We are generalizing a safety property born from a lived incident; the failure gets looked for, not assumed away.
- AS-24 WAL divergence + orphan message 161: two writers holding different views of one store, each locally self-consistent. The lanes topology (main-checkout .lattice/ vs N worktree copies of it) is the same shape in git; the two-plane rule is the mitigation, and the spike stress-tests it rather than trusting it.
- AS-26 rework cycle 2 (rate-limited implementer terminated mid-cycle, half-applied change left on disk): under lanes, a dying tick leaves TWO half-states. Resumability is an acceptance criterion below, demonstrated by killing a lane — not argued.

SHIPS CLEAN — the written result (docs/engineering/) must show pass/fail per criterion, with evidence:
(a) zero .lattice/ paths in git diff master...branch for BOTH trial branches;
(b) each worktree's diff confined to its own task's files; both worktrees and the main checkout clean at trial end;
(c) event-log integrity: every transition's from-state correct, no duplicate claims, comments attributed to their authoring employees;
(d) kill-one-lane resumability: a next tick resumes from .lattice/ state + lattice branch-link alone, and the surviving lane is unharmed;
(e) measured wall clock, fanned vs serial baseline;
(f) correct per-employee git identity on both branches.
Checker discipline per CLAUDE.md (AS-37/AS-53): every checker behind (a)–(c) must first be shown FAILING against a deliberately planted violation (scratch copy, never the task worktrees). A spike whose verdict gates a §9.8 decision does not rest on a green that was never seen red.

FIRST MEASURED PAIR (pre-agreed, record §9.5.3): Marcus on AS-41 (D1, Stripe Connect onboarding) + Lena on AS-34 (chat, /api/file symlink audit) — one D1 task + one chat task, maximally DISJOINT: different apps, zero shared files. Disjointness, not throughput, is the point of trial one: it isolates loop mechanics from merge mechanics while the lanes machinery is unproven, so any anomaly indicts the loop, not a merge seam. (It also happens to deliver the board's literal "one on chat, one on invoicing" on day one.) D1+D1 pairs — known edge contention: server route registration — come only after the disjoint trial ships clean, gated by a file-disjointness check on the concurrent pair. If the queue moves before the trial runs (e.g. AS-41 completes in the interleaved WIP=1 loop), substitute equivalents: the invariant is one-D1 + one-chat, maximally disjoint; the specific ids are the current instance.

§9.8 MEASUREMENT OBLIGATION (carried here so it cannot get lost): after lanes ship, the record-11 §3 overlap query must show a non-zero overlapping-pair count within one day OF RUNNING LOOP — and a count that stays 0 is itself a finding, returned to docs/strategy/11-second-developer-decision.md as a dated addendum. Clock discipline (the unstated-window defect is the §9.4(a) class; we are not writing another one): the one-day clock runs in loop-time, and a zero must be attributed — machinery-unused-at-dead-cadence is a cadence finding (rider §9.6.1), machinery-unused-despite-ticks is a lanes finding.

WHAT THIS TASK IS NOT
- It is NOT the lanes feature shipping. The deliverable is the written result + a proven prototype diff + exact proposed metawork wording. The production loop change is a SEPARATE follow-up task, filed by this spike only if the result says yes AND the board has had its veto window: the written result goes to #board before any Bounds/Operating-Modes wording changes, and silence is not treated as enthusiasm (record §4). Why the split: §9.8 makes the written result a re-decision input, and a decision point wants a completed artifact, not a task paused mid-lifecycle; the board's veto gate sits BETWEEN tasks, not inside one; and the experiment report and the production machinery change deserve separate reviews.
- It does not preempt the hires (already executed, record §9.1), does not touch running containers or the live watcher install, and runs under the CURRENT WIP=1 rules like any other task.
data.title: advance loop spike: parallel implementer lanes — WIP>1 under a single board writer

data.body: Filing notes (CTO). Dependency check at filing time: zero tasks in an active stage (board is all done/backlog/needs_human), so no depends_on edges recorded — checked, not assumed. Related but NOT dependencies: AS-27 (loop-status UI) renders a single-tick-in-flight concept that lanes would obsolete — its implementer should read this spike's result before building; AS-55 (watcher grant set) is watcher-adjacent but orthogonal. Sequencing per DM msg 427: this spike interleaves with Marcus's D1 spine work in the existing WIP=1 loop — it costs the spine roughly a handful of stages, it does not preempt it; if AS-41 or AS-34 close before the trial runs, the description's substitution invariant applies. Review recommendation: qa-ruben — he was hired for exactly this seam (concurrency, merge hygiene, parallel lanes), and reviewing the lanes spike is a better first task for him than any D1 item. AS-36 discipline applies doubly here: the spike's output IS a verdict, so no stage tasking message may contain the expected answer — hand the planner/implementer/reviewer the criteria and the file paths, never the conclusion.

Pulled as the highest-leverage task on the board: ~30 stage lifecycles remain in D1 v1 and WIP=1 is the only remaining term after cadence was fixed. I plan it as tech lead (the spike targets my own tick machinery); Lena implements — she was hired for exactly this surface (shared worktrees, merge hygiene, boundary discipline) and running the lanes trial is a fair first task for her. Ruben reviews, per the filing comment.

Plan written (CTO as tech lead). Architecture: lanes live INSIDE one tick — one manual lock-holding tick, one orchestrator as sole board writer, two implementer sub-agents in fenced worktrees; the two-concurrent-ticks alternative is rejected because it reintroduces the two-writer class (AS-24/dup-scoring shape) or makes the lock load-bearing. Trial: Marcus/AS-41 + Lena/AS-34, kill lane A at first-commit+one-poll (45-min backstop), resume in a separate normal tick from durable state alone. Pre-committed threshold, set before data exists: the fan pays iff R = (dA1+dB−W_T1)/min(dA1,dB) ≥ 0.5, power floor min(dA1,dB) ≥ 15 min else verdict capped at qualified, overhead > 10 min flags regardless. Checkers committed at tools/lanes/ with fixture-based falsification BEFORE the trial; result doc at docs/engineering/03-parallel-lanes-spike.md; follow-up files only on verdict yes + explicit #board green-light. 14 ACs.

Starting phase 1 (build) in .worktrees/AS-60 on feat/AS-60-parallel-lanes: the seven checkers under tools/lanes/, the fixture generator and node --test falsification suites, and tools/lanes/README.md. Falsification evidence lands at docs/engineering/03-parallel-lanes-spike/evidence/falsification/ before any trial-time green is trusted (plan §3 gate, §8). No board writes from the worktree; no trial conduct in this phase.

Phase 1 (build) complete on feat/AS-60-parallel-lanes — 4 commits: 1c2ae75 (seven checkers), 88f34d4 (falsification harness), 1744077 (README), 79c82f4 (evidence). 19 files, 2701 insertions, worktree clean, task status untouched per the gate.

FILES (lines): tools/lanes/ check-branch-clean.sh 64, check-confinement.sh 131, check-disjoint.sh 141, check-event-integrity.mjs 212, check-resume-preconditions.sh 166, compute-lane-metrics.mjs 293, check-git-identity.sh 91, README.md 173; test/ fixture.mjs 189 + 7 suites 1117; docs/engineering/03-parallel-lanes-spike/evidence/falsification/ 3 files 124.

SUITE: node --test 'tools/lanes/test/*.test.mjs' — 7 test files, 24 tests, 24 pass / 0 fail (~1.7s). Output committed at evidence/falsification/node-test-phase1.txt.

FALSIFICATION per checker (§8 contract: plant asserted applied via raw git/fs BEFORE the checker ran; failing set predicted in the assertion BEFORE the run; observed == predicted in ALL cases — no wider, no narrower):
(a) plant: committed .lattice/events file on a task branch (applied: raw diff lists it). Predicted+observed: exit 1, exactly that one path. Clean twin PASS, 'examined 2 changed file(s)'.
(b) plants x3: out-of-prefix commit; dirty worktree (applied: raw porcelain '?? apps/invoicing/scratch.txt'); dirty main checkout. Each exactly the 1 predicted item. Clean twin PASS.
(b') plants x2: overlapping prefix sets (applied: config read back, apps/shared/ in both tasks); one file in both branch diffs (applied: raw diffs). Exact matches. Clean twin PASS.
(c) plants x4: corrupted from-state; duplicate claim (from=null while held — AS-24 shape); in-window event with nearest ledger entry 90s (applied: nearest recomputed from raw files = 90s); mis-attributed in-window comment. Each exactly 1 predicted item. Clean twin (legal chains, legal reassignment, attributed+ledgered window) PASS 'examined 7 event(s) / 2 task(s) / 2 in-window / 2 attributed task(s)'.
(d) plant: branch_linked event removed — predicted failing set is TWO items {branch-link, worktree} by design (worktree exists on disk, asserted; the durable pointer to it is what is gone; semantics in README). Observed matched. Second plant: scaffold-shaped plan (heading + verbatim description) fails exactly {plan}. Clean twin PASS.
(e) plants: missing tB_spawn marker: hard FAIL, and asserted NO metric line printed (never fabricate); ledger divergence 90s on tA_kill: hard FAIL naming marker and seconds. Hand-computed twins reproduced EXACTLY, full 18-line output blocks asserted string-equal with event-id citations: R=0.6 fixture (dA1=40, dB=30, dA2=25, W_T1=52, overlap=18, savings=18, overhead=12, S0=95, fanned=77, S_real=105) and R=0.4 fixture (W_T1=58, overlap=12, savings=12, overhead=18, fanned=83) — one each side of the §9.2 threshold, identity self-check green in both.
(f) plant: commit authored developer-marcus-webb (the exact AS-53 drift; applied: raw git log author). Exact match. Second plant: canonical name, non-canonical email. Clean twin PASS.

REAL-TREE PROOF: every test file snapshots git status --porcelain of the containing tree before its tests and asserts byte-identical after — held on every run including the evidence capture. The guard itself was shown failing: a deliberately dirtying test in a scratch COPY under the session scratchpad (never the task worktree) trips the §8.4 assertion, exit 1 — committed as evidence/falsification/tree-guard-falsification.txt.

SELF-CHECK of this branch from the main checkout: (a) examined 19 changed file(s), PASS; (b) against AS-60's own config row (tools/lanes/ + docs/engineering/) examined 19 / 2 working tree(s), PASS including main-checkout-clean; (f) examined 4 commit(s), PASS (all developer-lena with canonical email). §15.11 confinement holds as of this comment.

DEVIATIONS / RECORDED INTERPRETATIONS:
1. The plan's literal runner command 'node --test tools/lanes/test/' (§8, §12, §15.1) does NOT run on host node v24.13.1 — node >= 23 no longer expands a directory argument (verified in an isolated minimal case; MODULE_NOT_FOUND on the directory). Canonical invocation is: node --test 'tools/lanes/test/*.test.mjs' (quoted; node expands). Documented in tools/lanes/README.md; §12's review tasking step 1 needs the same substitution.
2. compute-lane-metrics.mjs emits numbers only and applies NO §9.2 thresholds — §9.3 and phase 3 own ruler application; the measuring tool stays verdict-free.
3. S_real implemented literally per §9.1: S0 + median of consecutive company-wide status_changed gaps within the 24h wall-clock window ending at windows.T2.end, gaps >= 60 min excluded; even-count median = mean of the middle two; zero qualifying gaps prints 'S_real = n/a' and still passes (context metric). The script prints the exact filter it applied.
4. (c) ledger matching is time-only: an event is accounted for if ANY ledger entry lies within +/-60s (one-to-many allowed). Rationale: terse ledger notes stay usable and the planted stray still trips; documented in README as a known looseness.
5. (d) evaluates its four preconditions independently — with no branch-link the worktree precondition also fails ('no branch-link to match'); the two-item failing set is the pinned prediction, not an accident.
6. (b') gates ALL unordered pairs of config tasks (the spike's own row included), not only the lane pair — stricter than the minimum reading and the honest campaign shape; missing branch is exit 2 since the gate runs post-planning.
7. Extra plants beyond the plan's table minimums: (b) dirty-main, (c) mis-attribution, (d) scaffold plan, (e) ledger divergence, (f) non-canonical email — every pass-definition clause has now been seen red; none replaces a required plant.
8. This comment is posted directly by me per the orchestrator's phase-1 tasking ('from the main checkout: lattice comment ...'); plan §3 phase 1 anticipated relaying my breadcrumbs instead — flagging the mismatch rather than resolving it silently.
9. Size: tooling+tests ~2400 lines vs §17's 600-900 estimate. The §8 exact-string predictions and the extra plants are verbose; scope is exactly §2, nothing added.

PRE-TRIAL NOTES for the gate:
- (c) structural baseline over the REAL event log (2026-09-02, read-only, from main checkout): examined 574 event(s) / 60 task(s) / 0 in-window — PASS. The trial starts from a clean board baseline; any trial-time (c) FAIL is trial-caused, not historic noise.
- trial-config.json schema and the exact marker grammar are in tools/lanes/README.md. (e) prefix-matches exactly 'lanes-trial: lane spawned' / 'lane killed' / 'lane returned' per lane task per window and requires exactly one hit each — free text after the prefix is fine; ledger each marker within 60s of posting or (e) refuses the measurement.
- (e) exits 2 until BOTH windows carry recorded start+end, and needs all six markers, so it runs only after T2 — an A4 abort leaves it correctly refusing, which IS the 'not-measured' answer.
- Config worktree paths resolve relative to --repo; allowed_prefixes are plain string prefixes, end them with '/'.

PHASE 1 GATE — PASS. Verified as orchestrator, from the main checkout, before scheduling the trial (plan §3 gate). Cardinality first: 7 checkers present under tools/lanes/, 7 matching node --test suites plus fixture.mjs, 3 evidence artifacts committed. Suite re-run independently from a clean shell: 24 tests / 24 pass / 0 fail, and the main checkout porcelain was empty before and after. Committed evidence tally matches the re-run (tests 24 / pass 24 / fail 0). Every checker carries a planted violation with the plant asserted applied and the failing set predicted before the run; the tree-guard itself was falsified in a scratch copy, not the worktree. Branch carries 0 paths under .lattice/ (checker (a)'s own criterion, verified independently). Gate open: phase 2 may be scheduled. Carried into the trial from the implementer's report — (1) the canonical suite invocation is node --test 'tools/lanes/test/*.test.mjs' (node >= 23 stopped expanding directory args; the plan's literal form is a no-op on host node 24.13.1) and §12's review template must carry that substitution; (2) event-integrity ran structurally over the real log today at 574 events / 60 tasks PASS, so a trial-time FAIL is trial-caused.

Phase 3 (write) complete on `feat/AS-60-parallel-lanes`, commit `b69e81f` — `docs/engineering/03-parallel-lanes-spike.md`, 396 lines, all twelve plan §10 sections in order. Branch self-check from the main checkout: (a) 45 changed files PASS, (b) 45 files / 2 working trees PASS (confined to `tools/lanes/` + `docs/engineering/`), (f) 7 commits PASS. Worktree clean; no `.lattice/` writes and no `lattice` CLI writes from me.

VERDICT: qualified. Rulers applied mechanically, none moved. §9.2.1 R = 1.0000 >= 0.5 passes; §9.2.3 overhead 0.00 <= 10, no flag; §9.2.2 power floor TRIPS — min(dA1, dB) = dB = 9.45 min < 15 — capping the (e) verdict at "qualified — remeasure on a pair with both lanes >= 30 min". §9.2.4 clock discipline holds (3.72-min inter-tick gap excluded from every fan number). Scoreboard: 6 criteria / 7 checkers / 19 evidence files / 18 verdicts, 18 of 18 PASS, zero FAIL, every checker seen red in phase 1.

Two derived findings the doc rests on, both verified against the numbers rather than repeated from the ledger. (1) R and overhead are algebraically degenerate here: with tA_spawn == tB_spawn, W_T1 identically equals max(dA1,dB), so savings identically equals min(dA1,dB), R identically 1 and overhead identically 0 for ANY lane durations. R = 1.0000 records only that both spawn markers landed in the same second (163 ms apart in one batch). The informative orchestration cost is 5.34 min — the 33.16-min held lock minus the 27.82-min marker window — which is under the 10-min flag but is NOT the pre-committed metric and is not substituted for it. (2) Marker skew: markers posted 1.61 min before the actual spawn, lane B's return marker 2.30 min after it finished, so ~41% of measured dB is instrumentation (true runtime ~5.53 min) — the floor bites harder, not softer.

D2's consequences, stated more narrowly than the ledger did: the late kill invalidates the kill-timing datum AND the residue-case sample (poll log has dirty=1 at the on-time point 07:08:35Z, so the pre-committed clock would have sampled the dirty case; the AS-26 half-applied-change shape went untested) AND the strength of the resumability datum (1 of 3 commits and an incomplete implementation at the on-time point, so an on-time kill forces resume-by-continuation; what ran was resume-by-verification, zero new commits). It does not move R: under the on-time clock dA1 = 13.73 min > dB = 9.45, lane B still nests. §6.2.5's five clauses all hold, so criterion (d) passes in the sense the plan defined.

Two plan obligations were missed and are recorded as absences, not failures: 0 heartbeat entries in 50 ledger lines on a 33.16-min lock (acceptance §15.4 NOT met), 1 of >=4 lock ops ledgered, pid liveness sampled twice 12 s apart in setup only; and (b') never re-run post-T2 (plan §7's table and §6.2.4's step list disagree). Also: the §6.1.3 concurrency probe as written would have A1-aborted a healthy fan — lane A wrote no files for 8 minutes while reading.

Question 3 answered "no" empirically, not just arithmetically: apps/invoicing/ implementation p50 70.2 / p75 88.4 / max 381.3 min (4 of 5 over the whole 30-min budget alone); D1+D1 ~ 75.5 min; this trial's own fan held the lock 33.16 min with its D1 lane killed early. Only chat+chat fits, at a 14.3% per-fan risk of a lane alone blowing the budget. Lanes are live/supervised-manual only; changing that is watcher config + launchd plist together with lockStaleMin and the heartbeat interval, board-gated.

§9 is proposed wording, NOT APPLIED — advance.md step 0 asserted unchanged, plus exact replacement text for Bounds bullet 1, step 2's implementation bullet, and three CLAUDE.md insertions. §11 records that the filing gate needs verdict yes plus an explicit #board reply, and today's verdict is qualified, so the gate is not met; three courses are laid out for the board and CTO without choosing among them. §10 distinguishes the trial's own 9.45-min historical overlap from the §9.8 post-ship obligation and warns that the trial window must be excluded, plus a third possible attribution for a zero: lanes-are-supervised-only.

Findings from the lanes are attributed in §12: Marcus's two corrections to AS-41's plan §7 predictions (F1 and F2 failing sets wider than predicted; F2's stated rationale wrong — R6 trips on the due-list mapping, not the readiness flag) with his own remedy (fix the predictions, don't narrow the tests), and his durable-state guardrails gap now carried in AS-59; my two apps/chat/server.js conventions that a reformatting pass would silently break; and the stale `node --test tools/lanes/test/` invocation in plan §8/§12/§15.1 that §12's review template still needs substituted before Ruben runs it. Stale plan text listed at the end for the tech lead: §6.0.4, §7's --repo, §6.1.3, §7-vs-§6.2.4, and the runner command.

PASS — 12 of 14 acceptance criteria met, 2 not met (§15.4, §15.5's pre-committed kill clock), both self-disclosed by the document and both landing on trial conduct rather than on the deliverable. Not implementation-level rework, not plan-level rework. One inline fix committed (02f7200). Review by qa-ruben, fresh context, 2026-09-02.

READ ORDER AND INSTRUCTION-ORDER COMPLIANCE. Followed the tasking sequence exactly: (1) suite + falsification evidence, (2) metrics recomputed from .lattice/events/ + the ledger and WRITTEN DOWN before opening any measurement or verdict section, (3) checker re-runs, (4) verdict mechanics + §10 sections, (5) prompts + relay, (6) confinement. I read the plan, then the branch inventory, then ran the suite, then the event log and ledger, then my own recomputation — and only then the result document. I read the implementers' own reports (Lena's phase-1/phase-3 comments, Owen's gate comment) LAST, after my conclusions were formed. Two disclosures. (i) ANCHORING LEAK, minor but real: the phase-3 commit subject is "AS-60: write the parallel-lanes spike result — verdict qualified", so `git log` during my step-1 branch inventory showed me the verdict word before I recomputed anything. §12 binds the tasking message and the tasking message was clean; a reviewer's first action is nonetheless `git log`. My numbers were derived mechanically from event timestamps and the threshold application is arithmetic, so the exposure is bounded — but per AS-36 the damage is invisible afterward, so I state it rather than let it pass. Filed as finding 5. (ii) PRIOR CONTACT: I reviewed AS-34 (lane B's output) at 08:24Z today. That review sits entirely after T2's window closed (07:46:57Z), touched no spike artifact, and AS-34's code is not under review here — but a referee declares prior contact rather than being found to have had it.

CARDINALITY BEFORE QUANTIFICATION. Examined: 46 changed files / 8 commits on feat/AS-60-parallel-lanes (45/7 as submitted, +1/+1 from my inline fix); 7 checkers; 7 node --test suites + fixture.mjs; 20 committed evidence files carrying 18 verdicts; 616 events across 61 task streams; 2 trial windows; 3 archived prompts; 2 relayed breadcrumbs + 4 lanes-trial markers; 13 metric quantities + 6 source event ids; 14 acceptance criteria.

1. SUITE AND FALSIFICATION (instruction 1). `node --test 'tools/lanes/test/*.test.mjs'` from the spike worktree on node v24.13.1: 7 files, 24 tests, 24 pass / 0 fail. The plan's literal `node --test tools/lanes/test/` is indeed a no-op on node >= 23; the quoted-glob form is the canonical one and is already documented in tools/lanes/README.md and doc §12 residual 12. All 7 checkers carry committed falsification: (a) 1 plant, (b) 3, (b') 2, (c) 4, (d) 2, (e) 4, (f) 2 — each asserting the plant applied before the run and matching a failing set predicted before the run. I verified the suite's own real-tree guard independently rather than trusting its self-report: main-checkout and worktree `git status --porcelain` captured before and after the whole run were byte-identical (both empty). The guard itself has committed falsification — a deliberately dirtying throwaway test in a scratch COPY trips the §8.4 assertion with exit 1, with the scratch tree's porcelain proving the plant applied. Phase-1 evidence timestamps (commits 02:07–02:08 local = 06:07–06:08Z, gate 06:16:46Z) all precede T1's window start (06:54:38Z), so §15.2's ordering requirement holds.

2. INDEPENDENT RECOMPUTATION (instruction 2). Computed with my own script from .lattice/events/ + ledger, written before reading doc §5/§8; I deliberately did not read or import compute-lane-metrics.mjs first. RESULT: EXACT MATCH ON ALL 13 QUANTITIES AND ALL 6 EVENT IDS.
